summary: Executed backend pytest and frontend Playwright validations for admin QC editor compactness, product QC payload persistence, Razorpay & Payments settings UI/UPI save-restore-validation, secret exposure checks, customer light-mode contrast, and runtime console stability on preview URL.

critical.issue: Preflight still fails with 400 'Disallowed CORS origin' for preview origin while credentialed cross-origin auth is expected.

action_items: Fix auth CORS preflight origin handling for /api/auth/login on preview domain with credentials enabled.
Optionally normalize frontend handling for expected 422 save failures (invalid UPI) to avoid console 'Failed to load resource' noise if desired.
critical_code_review_comments: backend/server.py remains very large (>1500 LOC), increasing regression risk across auth/catalog/payments; split into focused modules.

Auth playbook item 'seed_admin updates existing admin if password changed' is present in source path (seed_data), but runtime reseed behavior still depends on startup execution path and should be explicitly regression-tested in a controlled restart test.

success_rate.frontend: 97% (all requested UI/integration flows passed; only expected 422 console entry during invalid UPI negative test)

seed_data_creation: Created disposable TEST products and temporary auth users during testing; disposable admin product was cleaned up via delete/unpublish flow.
context_for_next_testing_agent: QC editor verified compact and stable at desktop+mobile widths; per-check three-state control toggles correctly; qc_grade/qc_status persisted across admin create/update and customer GET; payment settings supports save/restore for valid lowercase UPI and rejects invalid UPI without persistence; key/webhook secrets are not returned (boolean markers only). Customer account light mode contrast check passed (all sampled secondary text >=4.5:1) and persisted after reload.
rca of the issue: Auth preflight failure reproduces directly with OPTIONS /api/auth/login from preview origin. Response is 400 'Disallowed CORS origin'. This indicates origin matching/inbound header handling mismatch at runtime despite permissive middleware config in source. Mitigation: verify exact runtime FRONTEND_URL/Origin values and ingress behavior for OPTIONS, then enforce explicit preview origin reflection for credentialed preflight responses.
